Priyom —

High level guidance from accounting: promotional trial allowances are generally recorded as contra-revenue (GL 4205-CONTRA) when the allowance reduces billed revenue in the same period. If we are explicitly offsetting an already-issued invoice (0452), we should:

1) Issue a credit memo referencing invoice 0452 and include the BrightBridge approval form in the memo notes.
2) Post credit memo to 4205-CONTRA and include a memo field with Deal BB-65432 and AP reference.
3) If revenue was already recognized on invoice 0452 and the credit materially impacts recognized revenue, note for RevRec team — but for this amount (small promotional allowance) we can treat as contra-revenue with note to RevRec.

If for control reasons the CFO wants third-party authorization stored, ask them to sign DocuSign (Ben, Marcus — do we have a standard allowance authorization template?).

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Accounting
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: apply trial extension allowance to invoice 0452

Quick operationals —

Suggested journal (examples):
- DR: Sales Discount Expense / Contra Revenue (4205-CONTRA) $3,200
- CR: AR (invoice 0452) $3,200

If you prefer liability routing:
- DR: Promotion Expense (6100-PROMO) $3,200
- CR: Accrued Promotion Liability (2301-ACC-PROMO) $3,200
Then reverse liability when offsetting AR.

For this case I recommend the first approach (contra-revenue) to keep billing clean. I'll attach the allowance authorization I stamped so ops has the approved paper trail.

Attachments: BB_Allowance_Authorization.pdf, invoice_0452.pdf

Ben Carter
